subject: Borealis - Dedicated GPU bundle & SLA proposal
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@borealis.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool proposal — initial bundle and throughput targets

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, I pulled together a couple of structured options for Borealis to evaluate:

Option A (Performance):
- 40 x A100-equivalent vGPU reserved pool (24/7 capacity)
- Throughput target: sustained 180 tokens/sec across 8 concurrent streams
- 12-month reserved commit, 10% list discount
- SLA: 99.95% uptime for serving plane, standard incident SLA

Option B (Balanced):
- 30 x A100-equivalent vGPU reserved pool with burst to 45 for 2 hours/day
- Throughput target: sustained 120 tokens/sec across 12 concurrent streams
- 12-month reserved commit, 18% list discount + one-time migration credit
- SLA: 99.9% uptime with higher-lookback SLO for throughput guarantees

We understand Borealis has a competing offer on the table. If you can share the rough band or structure (commit length / credits), we can propose a one-time strategic concession for new customers in your vertical. I attached the MQP spreadsheet with cost lines and a draft mutual action plan.

Next step: would love a quick call Thurs morning to walk the numbers and agree which option maps best to your Q3 roadmap.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0192

Attachments: 2027-04-21_Borealis_MQP_v1.xlsx
From: Elena Moreno <elena@borealis.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@borealis.ai>, Procurement <procurement@borealis.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 18:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool proposal — initial bundle and throughput targets

Hi Jasmine —

Appreciate the breakdown. High level feedback from our infra and product teams: Option B maps closer to our expected utilization for initial rollout, but we need firmer throughput SLAs (we cannot tolerate >10% degradation on peak batch inference).

A few clarifying asks:
1) Can you commit to a throughput SLA with credit-backed remediation?
2) We were offered a 22% discount by a competitor (12-month commit + 20% upfront credit). Can Redwood match or come close if we move faster?
3) Are there additional migration credits available if we sign before May 15?

Procurement also flagged that any executive concession must be documented with specific credit caps. Happy to sync tomorrow.

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Platforms | Borealis AI
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Borealis feedback — need exec approval for concession

Vivek —

Looping you in: Borealis is leaning to Option B but pushing for a deeper discount (they said 22% from a competitor) and a credit-backed throughput SLA. Procurement wants any concession to have a cap. Proposed asks:
- One-time migration credit capped at $75k if signed by 2027-05-15
- Increase discounted rate to 20% (from 18%) for a 12-month reserved commit
- Provide a throughput SLA: 99.8% for peak SLA with credit up to 5% of monthly invoice if missed (capped)

I attached the MQP and their rough usage profile. If we approve, I'd like to present a clean counter with capped credits and a staged rollout (pilot -> ramp) to mitigate risk.

Quick call would be great — are you available 9:30 PT?

Thanks,
Jasmine
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Borealis feedback — need exec approval for concession

Team —

Summary: I approve a targeted concession but with strict caps and gating. Approve the following on a conditional basis:
- 20% list discount for 12-month reserved commit (standard non-recurring revenue recognition)
- Migration credit: up to $50k (paid as invoice credit over first 2 months) if signed by 2027-05-15
- Throughput SLA: 99.8% with remediation defined as invoice credit equal to 3% of the monthly invoice for a single missed month, capped at $60k total over the contract year.

Conditions:
1) Product must sign off on the SLA language (Marissa, Ben please confirm measurability and runbook).
2) Legal to add explicit credit cap and charters in SOW.
3) Sales to build a ramp plan (pilot threshold before full reserved pool activation).

Marissa / Ben, please review and respond by EOD so I can get Legal looped.

Vivek
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Borealis feedback — need exec approval for concession

Vivek / team —

I can sign off on the SLA gating but want to tighten the measurement window and pilot criteria:
- SLA measurement: 5-minute rolling windows, measured at the edge serving tier; we can define token-per-second baseline and percentile (p95) measurement.
- Pilot: define a 6-week pilot at 30 vGPU equivalent with a throughput smoke test. If pilot passes, we flip to the 12-month reserved pool.
- Monitoring: include tracing hooks and a shared dashboard for both parties.

Assuming Legal takes the cap language, I’m good with the credits outlined. I recommend migration credit be invoiced as contra for month 1 and month 2 (25k / 25k) rather than a lump sum.

Ben
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@borealis.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@borealis.ai>, Procurement <procurement@borealis.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool proposal — Redwood counterproposal

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks. Following internal review, here is Redwood’s counterproposal (clean version for your procurement/legal):

- Bundle: Option B (30 vGPU reserved pool, burst to 45)
- Pricing: 20% discount off list on a 12-month reserved commit
- Migration credit: $50,000 (applied as $25k credit in month 1 and $25k in month 2) if contract signed by 2027-05-15
- Throughput SLA: 99.8% measured at p95 tokens/sec over 5-minute windows. If the SLA is missed, remediation is an invoice credit equal to 3% of the monthly invoice for the affected month. Total credit exposure capped at $60,000 for the year.
- Pilot: 6-week pilot at 30 vGPU equivalent with agreed smoke tests and shared dashboard. Full pool activation after pilot success.

Attached: mutual action plan (pdf) and updated MQP. If this matches Borealis’ needs, we can route a redlineable SOW and DocuSign within 48 hours.

Would you like a quick 30-minute call today to review language before procurement?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: borealis-mutual-action-plan.pdf, 2027-04-21_Borealis_MQP_v1.xlsx
